newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 31.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A much awaited increase in minimum wages following the recent hike in oil and power prices will be granted, but not until the first quarter of the coming year, an official of the regional wage and productivity board said. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Employees of Philippine Airlines staged a wildcat strike on Wednesday night, resulting in the cancellation of at least eight incoming international flights and five domestic flights. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Filipino-Chinese traders in Cotabato City closed shops on Wednesday to protest a series of kidnappings. The strike came after the foiled abduction of a Chinese couple on Tuesday in which the woman was killed. (MALAYA)

- President Fidel Ramos on Wednesday ordered Interior and Local Government Secretary Robert Barbers to mobilize special forces against kidnappers victimising businessmen in Metro Manila and Mindanao. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)

- Five star hotels in the Makati and Manila Bay area have reduced their rates to "reasonable levels" following complaints from delegates to the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum. There have been reports that hotels raised their rates in view of the large number of guests coming to Manila for the meeting. (THE MANILA TIMES)

- President Ramos and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl vowed to emhance the "new partnership" between Germany and the Philippines. Chancellor Kohl is in Manila on a three-day state visit. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- Socio-economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said that following the recent oil price hike, inflation in October was expected to rise to around 5.1 or 5.2 percent. In September, inflation was at 4.4 percent. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)

- The Philippine Stock Exchange is working out a plan with the Investment Houses Association of the Philippines that will guarantee an initial public offering allocation to all its member brokers, industry sources said. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)

- The initial public offering of Digital Telecommunications Phils Inc (Digitel), the only telecom firm to be listed on the stock exchange this year, has a drawn a favourable response from investors, the issue's lead underwriter PCI Capital Corp said. (THE MANILA TIMES)
- The National Power Corporation (Napocor) will float $150 million to $200 million worth of "Yankee" bonds in the U.S. within the next two months, Napocor sources said. (MALAYA)
